'''Yum-Tong Siu''' ({{lang-zh|t=蕭蔭堂}}; born May 6, 1943) is a Chinese mathematician. He is the William Elwood Byerly Professor of Mathematics at [[Harvard University]].

Siu is a prominent figure in the study of [[Function of several complex variables|functions of several complex variables]]. His research interests involve the intersection of complex variables, [[differential geometry]], and [[algebraic geometry]]. He has resolved various conjectures by applying estimates of the complex [[Neumann problem]] and the theory of [[multiplier ideal]] [[Sheaf (mathematics)|sheaves]] to algebraic geometry.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.msri.org/communications/books/Book37/index.html|title=MSRI Publications #37: Several Complex Variables|work=msri.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.asiapacific-mathnews.com/06/0601/0028_0034.pdf|title=Yum-Tong Siu: Hongkong-Princeton-Harvard, A Path of Several Complex Variables|work=Asia-Pacific Mathematics Newsletter}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Siu obtained his B.A. in mathematics from the [[University of Hong Kong]] in 1963, his M.A. from the [[University of Minnesota]], and his Ph.D. from [[Princeton University]] in 1966.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.shawprize.org/en/shawpage.php?tmp=1&twoid=3&threeid=98&pageid=38|title=Biographical Note of Professor Yum-Tong Siu|work=Shaw Prize|access-date=2016-11-17|archive-date=2017-06-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170612041235/http://www.shawprize.org/en/shawpage.php?tmp=1&twoid=3&threeid=98&pageid=38|url-status=dead}}</ref> Siu completed his doctoral dissertation, titled "Coherent Noether-Lasker decomposition of subsheaves and sheaf cohomology", under the supervision of [[Robert C. Gunning]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Siu|first=Yum-Tong|url=https://catalog.princeton.edu/catalog/1963991|title=Coherent Noether-Lasker decomposition of subsheaves and sheaf cohomology|date=1966|language=English}}</ref> Before joining Harvard, he taught at [[Purdue University]], the [[University of Notre Dame]], [[Yale]], and [[Stanford]]. In 1982 he joined [[Harvard]] as a professor, of Mathematics. He previously served as the Chairman of the Harvard Math Department.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.harvard.edu/index.html|title=Harvard Mathematics Department : Home page|work=harvard.edu|date=November 2024 }}</ref>

In 2006, Siu published a proof of the finite generation of the [[pluricanonical ring]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|eprint=math.AG/0610740|title=[math/0610740] A General Non-Vanishing Theorem and an Analytic Proof of the Finite Generation of the Canonical Ring|last1=Siu|first1=Yum-Tong|year=2006}}</ref>

==Awards, honors and professional memberships==
In 1993, Siu received the [[Stefan Bergman Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/prizes-awards/ams-supported/bergman-prize|title=Stefan Bergman Prize|work=American Mathematical Society}}</ref> of the [[American Mathematical Society]]. He has holds honorary doctorates from the University of Hong Kong, University of Bochum, Germany, and University of Macau. He is a Corresponding Member of the Goettingen Academy of Sciences (elected 1993); a Foreign member of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (elected 2004); and a member of the [[American Academy of Arts & Sciences]] (elected 1998),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.amacad.org/pdfs/alphaList09.pdf|title=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|work=amacad.org|access-date=2011-07-02|archive-date=2010-12-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101205200226/http://www.amacad.org/pdfs/alphaList09.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (elected 2002),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/275338121?pg=rslts|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120324091045/http://www.nasonline.org/site/Dir/275338121?pg=rslts|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 24, 2012|title=National Academy of Sciences|work=nasonline.org}}</ref> and [[Academia Sinica]], [[Taiwan]] (elected 2004).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://db1n.sinica.edu.tw/textdb/ioconas/02.php?func=22.1&_op=?ID:M107|title=院士會議|work=sinica.edu.tw}}</ref> He has been an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Helsinki]] (1978), [[Warsaw]] (1983) and [[Beijing]] (2002).

Currently, Siu is a member of the Scientific Advisory Board of the [[Clay Mathematics Institute]] (since 2003); the Advisory Committee for the Shaw Prize In Mathematical Sciences (since 2010);<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.shawprize.org/en/organization/structure/Siu.html|title=The Shaw Prize - Top prizes for astronomy, life science and mathematics|work=shawprize.org}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> the Advisory Committee for the [[Millennium Prize Problems]] under the sponsorship of the Clay Mathematics Institute; the Scientific Advisory Board for the [[Institute for Mathematics Sciences]], [[National University of Singapore]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.ims.nus.edu.sg/cv-sab.php|title=Institute for Mathematical Sciences (NUS)|work=nus.edu.sg|access-date=2011-07-02|archive-date=2012-11-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121122030620/http://www2.ims.nus.edu.sg/cv-sab.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> (since 2009) and the Institute of Advanced Studies, [[Nanyang Technological University]], [[Singapore]] (since 2006).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ntu.edu.sg/ias/panel/Pages/internationaladvisors.aspx|title=IAS: IAS Panel: International Advisors|work=ntu.edu.sg|access-date=2011-07-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322074957/http://www.ntu.edu.sg/ias/panel/Pages/internationaladvisors.aspx|archive-date=2012-03-22|url-status=dead}}</ref>
